author: Facundus of Hermiane

passages.original: An propterea factum non est quod iste adhuc per Ecclesiam catholicam sicut nunc docere non posset? aut potius quod necdum ad Ecclesiam catholicam devenisset qui hanc perversam atquc confusam ei vult inferre doctrinam, et utinam non Augustini nomine coloratam? Nam vult apostolicam scdem, quæ tunc aliis culpam dimisit, ipsam potius cum cæteris qui ejus in Acacio sententiam servaverunt, veluti pro facto schismate fuisse culpabilem; et more suo nemini purcens, illos quoque Orientales quibus petentibus dimissa est, videri vult ad schismaticos Occidentales fuisse conversos, quos ipsi ad se convertere debuerunt.
passages.english: Was it not done for this reason, that this man could not yet teach through the Catholic Church as he does now? Or rather, that the man who wishes to impose this perverse and confused doctrine on it, and would that it were not coloured with the name of Augustine, had not yet come to the Catholic Church? For he would have it that the apostolic see, which at that time forgave others their fault, was itself rather the guilty party, together with the others who kept to its sentence on Acacius, as though for having caused a schism. And, sparing no one in his usual way, he would have it appear that those Easterners too, who were forgiven at their own request, were converted to the schismatic Westerners, whom they themselves ought to have converted to themselves.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'atquc' for 'atque', 'scdem' for 'sedem', 'purcens' for 'parcens'.

passages.original: » Sed si forte cuiquam videtur illam tenere sententiam qua damnandi creduntur aJiqui in Ecclesiae pace defuncti, et non magis hanc apostolicx sedis quæ soli hæc intelligit divino judicio reservatum, et concesserit4quoniam si licct ligari mortuos, licet et solvi, et si licet mortuis damnationem inferre, licet et veniam dare : consequens non est ut ei propterea videatur etiam Mopsuestenus Theodotus esse damnandus. Non enim eos impetit illa sententia qui, sicut beatus Cyprianus cjusque socii, per humanam infirmitatem minus potuerunt ncie mentis abditiora penetrare, et veisimilitudine a veritate aberraverunt, sed eos potius qui probantur scientes volentesque peccasse.
passages.english: "But if perhaps someone thinks that he should hold that opinion by which some who died in the peace of the Church are believed to be subject to condemnation, rather than this opinion of the apostolic see, which understands these matters to be reserved to the divine judgement alone, and should grant that, since if it is permitted for the dead to be bound, it is permitted also for them to be loosed, and if it is permitted to inflict condemnation on the dead, it is permitted also to grant pardon, it does not follow that he must therefore also think that Theodore of Mopsuestia should be condemned. For that opinion does not strike at those who, like blessed Cyprian and his companions, through human weakness were less able to penetrate the more hidden things with the keenness of the mind, and strayed from the truth through what seemed probable, but rather those who are proved to have sinned knowingly and willingly.
passages.notes: Corrected scanning errors: 'aJiqui' (aliqui), 'apostolicx' (apostolicae), 'concesserit4' (stray mark removed), 'licct' (licet), 'cjusque' (ejusque), 'ncie' (acie), 'veisimilitudine' (verisimilitudine). 'Theodotus' is evidently an error for Theodorus (Theodore of Mopsuestia), as the following context confirms. The syntax of 'videtur... tenere... et concesserit' is loose; the rendering construes 'concesserit' as a second condition. The opening quotation mark appears to mark a quotation in the edition.
